title: Count Subsets (Minimum Subarrays)
statement:
You are given N positive integers.

You may rearrange the elements in any order.

Your task is to divide the array into the minimum number of subarrays such that, in each subarray, every element is greater than or equal to its 1-based index in that subarray.

If an element cannot satisfy the condition in the current subarray, start a new subarray.

### Input Format
- The first line contains an integer N representing the size of the array.
- The second line contains N space-separated positive integers.

### Output Format
- Print a single integer representing the minimum number of subarrays required.

examples.explanation: After sorting: [1, 2, 5, 5, 5]. 1-based indices [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. All elements satisfy arr[i] >= 1-based index. Total subarrays = 1.
After sorting: [1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 6, 6, 6]. Greedy partitioning creates 3 subarrays: [1], [1, 2, 3, 6], [1, 6, 6]. Total minimum subarrays = 3.

hints: Sort the array first to place smaller numbers at the beginning.
Maintain a 1-based target index starting at 1 for the current subarray.
For each element, if arr[i] >= current index, increment the index requirement.
If arr[i] < current index, start a new subarray (increment total count, reset index requirement to 1, and re-evaluate the current element).
discussion: Greedy sorting and index tracking approach.
